value.summary: Hearth — Bramblebridge and the places worth returning to - Visible question: can the party become part of a community without taking over its life? - Pressure: toll abuse, floods, work, small debts, strained institutions, and the changes caused by adventurers becoming locally important. - Recurring cast: Elowen Pike, Nessa Quill, Tibb Fallow, Merrit Vale, Della Crookshaw, Brother Odo, Fenna Dorr, Sera Lark, Jory Fenner. - Escalation if ignored: traders bypass town, the Kettle loses custom, mill debts rise, drainage work worsens floods, and Rusk's network becomes the only practical transport system. - Possible endings: a fair local freight charter; a community-run bridge house; Crown control; tolerated smuggling; or a hybrid system the party helps negotiate.

Crown — authority, succession, and the price of preventive control - Visible question: who should hold emergency power when lawful succession is uncertain? - Pressure: Queen Adela's undeclared heir, Chancellor Vane's centralization, provincial resentment, and rival interpretations of law. - Recurring cast: Queen Adela, Vane, Provost Drail, Crown councillors, Highmead scholars, foreign diplomats, Veyr succession figures. - Escalation if ignored: toll systems centralize, couriers become politicized, claimants seek foreign promises, and fear of war becomes justification for coercion. - Possible endings: declared heir; reformed succession law; regency compact; elective council; divided crown powers; or a crisis that the party helps keep peaceful without deciding who rules.

Road — independent adventures and cross-continent relationships - Visible question: what obligations arise simply because the party passes through? - Pressure: shipyards, orchards, rescue roads, festivals, lost messages, creature habitats, marriages, labour, local law, and people who need help for reasons unrelated to the main plot. - Recurring cast: Wayward Company, Roadmenders, couriers, shipwrights, cooks, ferrymasters, performers, scholars, and local hosts. - Escalation if ignored: problems resolve without the party, sometimes well and sometimes badly; later visits reflect that history. - Possible endings: a network of trusted roads and hosts; a famous but complicated reputation; local resentments; or a decision to settle and let some distant calls pass to others.

Deep history — who owns memory and obligation - Visible question: why are destroyed Concord seals returning? - Pressure: the Seventh Ledger, missing archives, false records, erased communities, dragons' historical roles, and the temptation to restore efficient systems without consent. - Recurring cast: Celyn Marr, Council of Margins, Pella Sorn, archivists, missing League Chair Ansel Daro, Ilyr Vaust, Sable Annek, community record keepers. - Escalation if ignored: institutions obey old forms automatically, people disappear legally, emergency powers normalize, and archive holders bargain separately with states. - Possible endings: destroy central control while preserving open standards; distribute archive custody; reform the Council; expose every record at great risk; entrust selected keepers; or let a new compact arise from negotiated local rights. ## Six-volume campaign shape

entities.name: Volume II — The Price of a Fair Road (levels 2–4)

value.summary: Volume II — The Price of a Fair Road (levels 2–4) The party travels to Merecross and Highmead through flood season. Drail appears to be the organizer of the toll scheme; court and civic stories reveal the succession problem without making the party royal kingmakers immediately. 1. A Standard with a Hollow Heart: the hidden debt list in the guild weight names favoured carriers and one innocent family. 2. The Provost's Exception: prove how Drail made local failure support central reform. 3. The Comedy Crown: recover a prop crown and dispatch without destroying a theatre company. 4. Three Bridges, Two Courts: keep flood response working while institutions fight jurisdiction. 5. The Heir in the Footnote: uncover a recent legal interpretation without deciding succession by document alone. Apparent completion: Drail loses office, reforms, bargains, flees, or testifies. Higher reveal: Chancellor Vane authorized the policy model but not every abuse. Fresh unrelated door: the flood damage…

entities.name: Volume III — Roads That Do Not Agree (levels 4–6)

value.summary: Volume III — Roads That Do Not Agree (levels 4–6) The party ranges across Eredane. Each region has its own problem; only some touch the Crown or Seventh Ledger. This volume prevents conspiracy fatigue and builds continental relationships. 1. The Ship That Must Sail: navigate the justified Gullstrand strike, planted sabotage, and looming grain deadline. 2. The Grey Orchard Wife: address pale-canker, lost water rights, and a spirit story that may preserve legal memory. 3. The Shepherd Who Refused: protect a Veyr election from violence without forcing the best mediator to accept power. 4. The Choir Below Stone: explore Copperdeep's sealed levels and choose what evidence to surface. 5. The Wrong Rescue Contract: cooperate or compete with the Wayward Company after both parties are hired for different missing travellers with the same name. 6. A Funeral in Good Voice: honour war dead while exposing a forged veteran claim hidden in a choir competition. Higher main-thread reveal: Vane use…

entities.name: Volume IV — Across the Lantern Sea (levels 6–7)

value.summary: Volume IV — Across the Lantern Sea (levels 6–7) Travel to Solasca expands the World before the deepest plot becomes dominant. The journey includes shipboard comedy, genuine danger, and several unrelated social obligations. 1. A Wedding, If Convenient: find Cook Berto, resolve labour obligations, and decide whether hidden treaty clauses should become public before the ceremony. 2. The Compass of an Unbuilt Ship: investigate Tavaros's returned compass and its future date. 3. Three Resignation Letters: find missing League Chair Ansel Daro and determine which anticipated kidnapper received which letter. 4. The Flowers Inside the Sealed Hall: enter or observe the former Concord chamber without surrendering its archive to one state. 5. The Dry Sock Accounts: protect mutual-aid records that accidentally prove a courier network. Apparent completion: Celyn's Aster Quay cell is dismantled or divided. Higher reveal: Celyn answers to the Council of Margins, whose factions disagree. Fresh unr…

entities.name: Volume V — Names That Went Missing (levels 7–9)

value.summary: Volume V — Names That Went Missing (levels 7–9) The party moves through Namarra, Kethria, Tessarane, and Ordelain. Deep-history clues accumulate, but each polity's crisis retains independent stakes. 1. The Village That Is Not There: restore, conceal, or transform the legal status of an erased community without exposing it to predatory collection. 2. Seed for the Wrong Season: trace stolen durable seed through royal and private granaries. 3. The Doubled Tithe: expose the fraudulent copper demand and confront the reality of Kethria's dragon bargain. 4. The Ordinary Comet: protect honest observation from three politically useful prophecies, then discover one genuinely impossible detail. 5. The River Returns: mediate claims around Old Aur Island and recover records older than the Concord. 6. The Reed Graves: meet or outwit Sable Annek, who hoards legal absences rather than gold. Apparent completion: the Council's restoration plan becomes visible and several cells can be defeated. Hig…

entities.name: Volume VI — The Margins of Peace (levels 9–10)

value.summary: Volume VI — The Margins of Peace (levels 9–10) The final volume is a struggle over institutions, history, and custody rather than a march toward one required battle. The party can seek Ilyr, convene witnesses, expose records, bargain with states, split the Council, or build a replacement practice from relationships earned throughout the campaign. 1. The Council of Margins: reach, infiltrate, expose, debate, or fracture the transcontinental leadership. 2. The Archive That Answers Back: enter Ilyr's Listening Caves, where testimony contradicts official history and echo riddles test whether visitors listen rather than merely collect. 3. The Queen's Empty Chair: resolve Alderwick's succession pressure without allowing emergency policy to decide it silently. 4. The Accord Congress: keep delegates present and safe while each tries to control the archival settlement. 5. Ladder A — the toll conspiracy text Fara Dint, visible enforcer (coerced official, not true boss) → Rusk Pettifer, local organizer and Volume I apparent boss → Provost Halwen Drail, regional policy sponsor and Volume II apparent boss → Chancellor Sera Vane, national authority using the policy to prevent succession crisis → Auditor Celyn Marr, Seventh Ledger adviser shaping Vane's evidence → Council of Margins, distributed transcontinental leadership → Ilyr Vaust's historical responsibility and falsely invoked authority Every step can end through exposure, reform, removal, bargaining, defection, legal defeat, flight, or violence as fiction and supported mechanics permit. A higher reveal never restores a defeated lower actor's control automatically.

Ladder B — the shipyard sabotage text frightened apprentice caught damaging a fitting → private safety inspector paying for staged evidence → royal procurement broker trying to break the strike → grain speculator expecting delayed convoys and higher prices This ladder is independent of the Seventh Ledger. The “higher boss” is commercial leverage and a small network of respectable interests. The strike can end through negotiated safety, alternate shipping, public proof, worker control, or coercion with lasting consequences.

Ladder C — the missing villages text Emon Saar, boastful shell merchant who looks guilty → tax flotilla officers moving unrecorded grain → canal officials who erased villages to protect them during an old purge → current brokers exploiting that invisibility → Sable Annek, purchasing names and legal absence for a dragon archive The apparent criminals include protectors, exploiters, and people trapped between. Restoring every name publicly may expose households to debt; preserving invisibility may deny rights and services.
The recovered horse's tack carries orchard fungus, leading later to Bellafont—not to the toll plot.
